definition: An iterative execution cycle where a language model observes environment state, reasons over trajectories, issues tool calls, and adjusts actions dynamically.
details: Unlike single-turn generation, agentic loops maintain internal scratchpads to recursively query retrieval engines, code interpreters, or external APIs until a terminal condition or target goal is satisfied.
story: Think of a chess player who never commits to a move blindly — they consider the board, try an action, watch what changes, and only then decide what is next. The machine stops just answering one question and starts getting a job done, step by step, checking its work along the way. It plans a little, acts a little, looks at the result, and then decides what to do next. It is a loop of look, act, and learn — the same way you cook from a recipe you have never tried: add, taste, correct. And that habit of checking, acting, then checking again is Agentic Loop.

citation.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
